# Golf Cart Maps

> Golf Cart Maps (golfcartmap.com) is a golf cart and LSV (low-speed vehicle) map and route planner, now in beta. It shows which roads are legal for golf carts and street-legal LSVs in 37 beach and golf towns across the U.S., plans routes that stay on them, and cites the state law behind each rule.

URL: https://golfcartmap.com/

## What it does
- Colors every road: green = allowed for your vehicle, red = too fast or banned (avoid).
- Plans routes on allowed roads; crossing a faster road at an intersection is allowed where state law permits it.
- Battery range check for a trip, public EV chargers, and a way to report a wrong road.
- Works in a web browser; an iPhone app is in App Store review.

## State rules used
- Alabama: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (Single app rule ≤35 (Code of Ala. 32-1-1.1 LSV); Gulf Shores/Orange Beach region cap ≤25 (regions.json rule)). Golf carts: No state golf-cart road statute; local ordinance (Gulf Shores Sec. 21-13, Orange Beach Sec. 70-273: streets ≤25 mph).
- Arizona: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (A.R.S. 28-966 (NEV/LSV ≤35)). Golf carts: Arizona: golf carts must be registered/insured to use public streets; local police guidance (e.g. Marana PD) allows streets ≤35 mph. Sun City: A.R.S. 28-721(C) keep right. UNCONFIRMED.
- California: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (CVC 21260). Golf carts: CVC 21716 (golf carts only on highways posted ≤25 mph, within a business/residence district); CVC 21115 + Streets & Highways Code §1950-1965 golf cart transportation plans may designate other routes.
- Florida: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (F.S. 316.2122). Golf carts: F.S. 316.212(1) (golf carts only on roads a county/city has designated and signed, based on speed and traffic); 316.212(6)-(8) daylight unless equipped; 316.2126 municipal use. FLHSMV/FDOT guidance cites designated roads posted ≤30 mph; app uses the designation (≤35) and flags this. UNCONFIRMED.
- Georgia: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (O.C.G.A. 40-6-362). Golf carts: O.C.G.A. 40-6-331 (PTVs only where a local ordinance allows); app uses the common local cap of ≤25 mph (Glynn County, Tybee, Peachtree City streets except Hwy 74/54/Peachtree Pkwy). UNCONFIRMED per town.
- Hawaii: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (HRS 291C-134 (neighborhood electric vehicles: roads posted ≤35 mph, may cross at intersections, no controlled-access highways); HRS 291C-53). Golf carts: HRS 291C-134 (only neighborhood electric vehicles), HRS 286-2 (golf carts not registrable motor vehicles).
- Maine: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (29-A M.R.S. §2089 (LSVs on roads posted ≤35 mph, may cross at intersections); §501(2-A) golf carts only on islands without state roads). Golf carts: 29-A M.R.S. §501(2-A) (golf carts only on islands without state roads); §2089 LSVs.
- North Carolina: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (N.C.G.S. 20-121.1 (LSV ≤35); golf carts by local ordinance (G.S. 160A-300.6)). Golf carts: N.C.G.S. 160A-300.6 / 153A-245 (golf carts only where a town/county ordinance allows); app uses the most common cap of ≤25. UNCONFIRMED per town.
- Ohio: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (ORC 4511.214 (under-speed/LSV on ≤35 roads where locally authorized; Put-in-Bay village permits carts)). Golf carts: ORC 4511.214 (under-speed vehicles on roads ≤35 mph where the local authority allows; titled, inspected, plated); Put-in-Bay Codified Ord. 490.02.
- South Carolina: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (S.C. 56-5-820). Golf carts: S.C. 56-2-105 (secondary roads posted ≤35 mph, within 4 mi of registration address, daylight unless local ordinance; permit + decal).
- Texas: LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less (Tex. Transp. Code 551.304 (NEV/LSV on roads ≤45; app uses ≤35)). Golf carts: Tex. Transp. Code 551.403-551.404 (golf cart plate required, 551.402; daytime on roads ≤35 within 2 mi of where parked or in a master-planned community, or where the city/county authorizes).

## How rules are sourced
Priority: manual fixes from local reports, then posted speed-limit signs seen in Mapillary street imagery, then official city speed lists and ordinances, then OpenStreetMap speed tags. Small residential streets without a posted limit are assumed to be 25 mph. Not legal advice; posted signs win.
